source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool user disable <User ID>` and check the user list.
source_snapshot.criteria: The disabled account has no privilege to access BMC, then the account is EMPTY after removal by Web UI.
source_snapshot.script: Internal `useraccount_delete` path whose exact revision and implementation are unavailable here.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL silently adds `user set name <ID> ""`, exposes the management password with `-P`, hard-codes cipher suite 17, does not execute the Criteria-required WebUI removal, and equates disable/name clearing/delete/empty without authoritative proof.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly separates disabled, deleted and empty states and requires a scratch identity, recovery path, channel/session evidence and supported removal, but leaves the explicit source Criteria framed as a choice rather than two required sequential checkpoints.

old_problem: The title says Delete, the Procedure contains only an IPMI disable, and Criteria separately require loss of BMC access plus an empty slot after WebUI removal. Earlier reviews treated disable-only, delete-only and two-phase execution as alternatives, while DeepSeek invented username clearing. This left the test decision pending and risked false deletion evidence or removal of a protected account.
disposition_reason: The source Criteria determine the full coverage: first execute the preserved IPMI disable and prove access denial; then execute an actual vendor-supported WebUI removal and prove the same numeric slot is empty. These are sequential independent checkpoints, not substitutes. Exact WebUI controls, channel/session behavior and target mappings are Project bindings. DeepSeek's name-clear command is excluded because it is neither the source Procedure nor visual WebUI removal.
decision_basis: XLSX row 941, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 942 were directly reviewed; the next identity was verified as Functionality row 942 / variant b43aa3b43b1e555a.

Criteria 1 explicitly attaches denial to the IPMI disable and Criteria 2 explicitly attaches EMPTY to removal by Web UI. Reading them as two ordered acceptance checkpoints preserves both statements and the title without choosing one operation over another.

Pinned upstream ipmitool source implements user disable through the Set User Password enable/disable operation and separately retrieves username/access fields; it does not define disable as erasing the user name or channel access. Disable evidence therefore cannot satisfy empty-slot evidence.
The user's approved WebUI rule requires the actual UI operation and visual evidence. An API, `user set name ""`, list-only check or internal script cannot replace the WebUI checkpoint.
ED-03/ED-13 and ED-33 through ED-38 permit a standard command contract plus Project-specific UI/session bindings while preserving source operations, safety gates and engineer-owned DUT verdict.

test_case.test_name: Disable one disposable IPMI account, prove access denial, then remove it in WebUI and prove the numeric slot is empty
test_case.purpose: Verify two distinct source requirements on one approved disposable account: the IPMI disable command prevents BMC access, and a subsequent real WebUI removal deletes the account so its numeric IPMI slot is empty, without changing protected users, unrelated channel access, SOL entitlements or recovery access.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware/WebUI identity, pinned supported ipmitool version, protected RMCP+ and WebUI administrator credential paths, approved cipher/TLS policy
Dedicated disposable account with immutable numeric user ID, known protected test secret, relevant channel/access/SOL mappings and a successful bounded pre-disable login
Protected/root/break-glass account list, already-open independent recovery administrator session and complete per-channel/session baseline
Project/vendor definition of post-disable new-login denial and existing-session invalidation/authorization behavior
Pinned vendor WebUI removal workflow, account-to-IPMI-slot mapping, confirmation text, expected visual empty/absent state and proof that removal is supported
Two separate point-of-action approvals: IPMI disable first, WebUI removal second after disable evidence is accepted
Screenshot/redaction, audit retention and final empty-slot/no-unrelated-change evidence plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL SECURITY WRITE WITH MANUAL VISUAL CHECKPOINT. Preserve logs. From an independent recovery session, prove the target ID is the dedicated disposable account on every relevant channel and capture user/access/SOL/session baselines plus a successful bounded pre-disable login. After approval 1, run `ipmitool ... user disable <ID>` once without `-P`, then immediately capture complete explicit-channel user/access/SOL state, audit event, a new protected login denial and the Project-defined existing-session result; do not clear the name or call this deletion. After that checkpoint is accepted and approval 2 is recorded, a human or approved browser workflow must open the pinned BMC WebUI, visually confirm target BMC plus immutable ID/name, capture the pre-delete account row/details, invoke the vendor Remove/Delete control for only that account, capture confirmation and completion, refresh/re-login as necessary, and capture the account's absence/empty visual state. From the recovery session, re-run complete explicit-channel inventory and prove the same numeric slot is empty and all protected/unrelated users remain unchanged. Do not substitute API-only evidence, `user set name <ID> ""`, disable-only evidence or the unreviewed internal script.
test_case.expected_result: Checkpoint A: the one disposable account is disabled, new authentication is denied, existing-session behavior matches the approved security contract, and no unrelated account/access/SOL state changes; its identity may still remain visible and must not be called deleted. Checkpoint B: the actual WebUI removal completes for that same immutable identity, visual evidence shows the account absent/empty, explicit-channel IPMI inventory shows the intended slot empty under vendor semantics, relevant access/SOL entitlements are removed, recovery/protected accounts remain usable and audit evidence records only the approved target.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires both checkpoints independently: one exact IPMI disable with proved access denial/session behavior, followed by a separately approved actual WebUI removal with visual evidence and authoritative empty-slot proof for the same ID. Disable or list output alone cannot pass; name clearing cannot substitute for WebUI deletion; API evidence may only corroborate. Wrong identity, retained access contrary to policy, missing visual evidence, non-empty final slot, unrelated-account delta, secret exposure or recovery impairment is FAIL and stops. Missing target/UI/channel/session bindings is NOT READY rather than Engineering Decision Pending; documented absence of a supported WebUI delete may produce N/A only with authoritative applicability evidence, never disable-only PASS.
safety_gate: Use only a pre-provisioned disposable account; correlate immutable ID, name and relevant channels and exclude root, fixed, production, owner and recovery identities before each write.
Keep an independent recovery administrator session. Obtain separate approvals for IPMI disable and later WebUI removal; execute each once and never automatically retry a failed or ambiguous action.
Never put management or target-account passwords in `-P`, arguments, logs, screenshots or records; preserve and redact security/audit evidence instead of clearing it.

After disable, stop if the wrong slot changed, protected access changed, new authentication still succeeds contrary to policy, or existing-session state is unexplained. Do not proceed to deletion merely to hide a failed checkpoint.
At WebUI removal, visually re-verify target BMC and account identity immediately before confirmation. Do not bulk-delete, use API-only substitution or infer success from a toast/request status.
Do not run DeepSeek's `user set name <ID> ""` or the internal script as deletion. Empty status must follow the supported WebUI removal and be proven by visual plus independent inventory evidence.
expected_evidence: Approval 1, target/BMC/ipmitool/WebUI identity, protected-account list, immutable disposable ID, complete per-channel access/SOL/session baseline and successful protected pre-disable login
Single IPMI-disable status/audit record, explicit-channel post-disable state, new-login denial and approved existing-session result
Approval 2 and actual WebUI screenshots/video artifacts showing target/account identity, removal confirmation, completion and refreshed absent/empty state with timestamps/hashes
Complete post-removal per-channel inventory proving the same numeric slot empty and access/SOL entitlements removed, with API/audit correlation only as supplementary evidence
Protected/unrelated account and recovery continuity, preserved logs, no secret exposure and engineer PASS/FAIL/N/A verdict for both checkpoints
test_case.recovery: At any mismatch, stop further writes and preserve evidence. Use the independent recovery account to keep management access, confirm which immutable ID changed and isolate the test session. If disable affected the wrong account, restore only from the approved captured account/access/SOL baseline with separate authorization; if WebUI deleted the wrong account, do not improvise a recreation because secrets/role mappings may be unrecoverable—invoke the vendor/project account-recovery procedure. The intended disposable account ends empty after a successful test, so no recreation is required.

source_conflict.reason: Procedure and Criteria define complementary ordered coverage: IPMI disable/access denial first, then WebUI removal/empty-slot proof. Treating the explicit criteria as two checkpoints preserves every source statement and removes false equivalence without modifying Master.

blocked.reason: The core operations and acceptance states are explicit. Exact vendor UI controls, account mapping, session policy and credentials are finite Project/package prerequisites.

project_authority: The Project/vendor package binds the WebUI workflow and slot mapping, defines existing-session expectations and authoritative empty semantics, supplies protected identities and owns the two-checkpoint verdict. Lack of these runtime bindings prevents execution but does not leave the review decision unresolved.
